messages.content: You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My wifi shows connected but there is no internet

The adapter had no DNS server assigned and a stale DHCP lease. Flushing the DNS cache, restarting the Wi-Fi adapter, and renewing the IP lease restored connectivity (ping to 8.8.8.8 now succeeds).
Commands used:
- Test-NetConnection 8.8.8.8 -InformationLevel Quiet
- Get-DnsClientServerAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select-Object InterfaceAlias, ServerAddresses
- Clear-DnsClientCache
- Restart-NetAdapter -Name 'Wi-Fi'
- ipconfig /renew
- Test-NetConnection 8.8.8.8 -InformationLevel Quiet
Recommendation: If this recurs after sleep, update the Wi-Fi driver from the vendor site.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Websites won't load but ping to IP addresses works - looks like DNS is broken

Name resolution was failing because the configured DNS server was unreachable. Setting Cloudflare/Google DNS (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8) and flushing the cache restored domain resolution.
Commands used:
- Resolve-DnsName microsoft.com -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
- Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceAlias 'Wi-Fi' -ServerAddresses ('1.1.1.1','8.8.8.8')
- Clear-DnsClientCache
- Resolve-DnsName microsoft.com | Select-Object -First 1 Name, IPAddress
Recommendation: Keep DNS set to automatic unless your network requires a specific resolver.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in bluetooth problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My bluetooth headphones will not pair with the laptop

The Bluetooth Support Service (bthserv) was stopped, so the pairing UI could not discover devices. Setting it to Automatic and starting it brought the stack online and the headphones paired.
Commands used:
- Get-Service bthserv | Select-Object Name, Status, StartType
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Bluetooth | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
- Set-Service bthserv -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service bthserv
- Get-Service bthserv | Select-Object Status
Recommendation: Put the headphones in pairing mode (hold the power button until the LED blinks) before adding them in Settings.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in bluetooth problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
The bluetooth toggle disappeared from Windows settings completely

The Bluetooth radio device was in an Error/Disabled state, which removes the toggle from Settings. Re-enabling the PnP device restored the radio and the toggle reappeared.
Commands used:
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Bluetooth | Select-Object Status, InstanceId
- Enable-PnpDevice -InstanceId 'USB\VID_8087&PID_0026\5&...' -Confirm:$false
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Bluetooth | Select-Object Status
Recommendation: If the toggle vanishes again after updates, reinstall the Bluetooth driver.

You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows (audio) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Microphone is connected but no apps can hear my voice

Microphone privacy setting was set to Deny, blocking all desktop apps from accessing the audio input. Changing the registry capability key to Allow restored microphone input.
Commands used:
- Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore\microphone' -Name Value
- Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore\microphone' -Name Value -Value 'Allow'
Recommendation: Check Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone if specific apps still fail.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in file (storage) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
USB flash drive plugged in but not showing in File Explorer

The USB flash drive partition had no mount point or drive letter assigned. Assigning drive letter E: mounted the volume and made it accessible in File Explorer.
Commands used:
- Get-Volume | Where-Object DriveLetter -eq $null
- Get-Volume -FileSystemLabel 'USB_DRIVE' | Get-Partition | Set-Partition -NewDriveLetter 'E'
Recommendation: Ensure USB drives are formatted as FAT32 or NTFS for auto-mounting.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
High latency and high ping spikes in online games over Wi-Fi

Periodic background Wi-Fi network scanning by WLAN AutoConfig caused ping spikes. Temporarily disabling autoconfig stopped background scans during active connections.
Commands used:
- netsh wlan show autoconfig
- netsh wlan set autoconfig enabled=no interface='Wi-Fi'
Recommendation: Remember to re-enable autoconfig when switching Wi-Fi networks.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Task Scheduler error prevents automated backup task from running

The Task Scheduler service (Schedule) was unexpectedly stopped. Starting the service enabled scheduled tasks to run normally.
Commands used:
- Get-Service Schedule | Select-Object Status, StartType
- Start-Service Schedule
Recommendation: Ensure Task Scheduler startup type remains on Automatic.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Cannot connect to local development server on port 8080

The local application was bound and listening on port 8080, but incoming local network traffic was blocked by Windows Firewall. Created an inbound firewall rule for TCP port 8080.
Commands used:
- Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8080 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
- New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Dev Server 8080' -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 8080 -Protocol TCP -Action Allow
Recommendation: Remove this rule if you stop running the local server.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
CPU is pinned at 100% by 'Windows Modules Installer Worker' for hours

TiWorker.exe (Windows Modules Installer Worker) was actively processing a pending update payload in the background, which is CPU-intensive but expected -- it is not malware.
Commands used:
- Get-Process TiWorker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, CPU
- Get-Service TrustedInstaller | Select-Object Status
Recommendation: Let it finish (usually 20-60 minutes); if it never completes, run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' to repair the underlying update components.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
PC slows down noticeably after 10-15 minutes of heavy use, like it's throttling

The processor's current clock speed had dropped well below its rated maximum during sustained load, consistent with thermal throttling protecting the chip rather than a software fault.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object Name, CurrentClockSpeed, MaxClockSpeed
Recommendation: Clean dust from the heatsink/fans and reapply thermal paste if the laptop/PC is a few years old; check Task Manager's Performance tab for temperature if your model exposes it.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Task Manager only shows 2 cores active even though the CPU has 8

Windows itself only sees 2 physical cores, which points to cores being disabled at the firmware level (BIOS/UEFI core count limit) rather than anything Windows can toggle.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object NumberOfCores, NumberOfLogicalProcessors
Recommendation: Enter BIOS/UEFI setup and check for a 'core limit' or 'active cores' setting under CPU configuration; reset it to 'all cores' or 'auto'.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
The CPU fan runs at full speed constantly, even when idle

CPU load itself is essentially idle, so the constant full-speed fan isn't a software load issue -- it points to a fan-curve setting stuck at 100%, often after a BIOS update or manual utility change.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object LoadPercentage
Recommendation: Check the fan curve in BIOS/UEFI or the vendor's fan-control utility and reset it to the default/auto profile.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
SysMain process uses a lot of CPU right after every boot

SysMain (Superfetch) was pre-loading frequently used apps into RAM right after boot, causing a short CPU/disk burst that tapers off within a couple minutes -- expected behavior, not a fault.
Commands used:
- Get-Service SysMain | Select-Object Status, StartType
Recommendation: If the burst is unacceptably long, disable SysMain, though on most modern SSDs it's safe to leave enabled.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
A generic svchost.exe process is using 40% CPU nonstop

The svchost.exe instance hosting the Update Orchestrator Service (UsoSvc) was scanning/staging Windows updates in the background, accounting for the sustained CPU use.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Where-Object ProcessId -eq 4820 | Select-Object Name, DisplayName
Recommendation: This normally finishes on its own; if it runs for many hours, restart the UsoSvc service or run the Windows Update troubleshooter.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
CPU never boosts to its rated speed, everything feels sluggish

The system was running on the Power Saver plan, which caps maximum processor state well below the CPU's rated boost speed. This is a configuration choice, not a hardware problem.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object CurrentClockSpeed, MaxClockSpeed
- powercfg /getactivescheme
Recommendation: Switch to the Balanced or High Performance power plan, or check 'Maximum processor state' under advanced power settings if it's capped below 100%.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Random CPU spikes cause stutter in games even on a powerful CPU

A background telemetry/update-check process was spiking periodically and stealing CPU time slices from the game, causing the stutter -- not a GPU or game-engine issue.
Commands used:
- Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 Name, CPU
Recommendation: Disable or delay unnecessary background telemetry/updater tasks via Task Scheduler while gaming.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
PC suddenly shuts off completely during heavy load, like a game or render

Event ID 41 (Kernel-Power) confirms the system lost power abruptly rather than shutting down cleanly, consistent with a thermal or power-protection shutdown under heavy CPU load.
Commands used:
- Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; Id=41} -MaxEvents 3
Recommendation: Check CPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool, clean/reapply cooling, and verify the PSU has enough headroom for the CPU's power draw.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Performance feels inconsistent, like only some CPU cores are being used

Core parking was configured to keep up to half the logical cores parked to save power, which throttles multi-threaded performance under the active power plan.
Commands used:
- powercfg /q SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_PROCESSOR CPMINCORES
Recommendation: Set 'Minimum processor state' and core-parking minimum to 100% under the power plan's processor power management settings if you want full multi-core performance.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
One old 32-bit app pins a single CPU core to 100% and makes the whole PC feel slow

The legacy app is single-threaded and doesn't spread work across cores, so it maxes out one logical core (visible as ~12% total on an 8-core CPU) while that core-bound operation feels slow.
Commands used:
- Get-Process OldApp -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, CPU, Id
Recommendation: Check for an updated, multi-threaded version of the app; setting its process priority to Below Normal can reduce its impact on the rest of the system.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
SearchIndexer.exe uses high CPU for a long time after copying a huge folder of files

Windows Search is indexing the large batch of newly added files so they become searchable, which is expected one-time CPU use that will taper off once indexing catches up.
Commands used:
- Get-Process SearchIndexer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object CPU
Recommendation: If it never settles, exclude rarely-searched folders (like large media archives) from indexing under Indexing Options.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
CPU-heavy tasks got noticeably slower after a Windows feature update

Virtualization-based Security (Credential Guard/HVCI) was enabled by the feature update, which adds a small but real CPU virtualization overhead to every process -- a known security trade-off, not a fault.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/Microsoft/Windows/DeviceGuard -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard | Select-Object VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus
Recommendation: If the overhead isn't acceptable for your workload, VBS can be turned off under Core Isolation settings, though this reduces protection against credential-theft malware.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
wmiprvse.exe periodically spikes CPU to 100% for a minute at a time

A monitoring or security tool was issuing frequent, heavy WMI queries, which spins up WmiPrvSE.exe hosts that briefly spike CPU while they run.
Commands used:
- Get-Process WmiPrvSE | Select-Object CPU, Id
Recommendation: Check installed monitoring/inventory agents for an overly frequent polling interval and increase it if configurable.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Just having a browser open with a few tabs uses a surprising amount of CPU

Several tabs are running heavy JavaScript (ads, auto-playing video, and on some sites cryptomining scripts) that individually don't look like much but add up across tabs.
Commands used:
- Get-Process chrome | Select-Object -First 5 Name, CPU, Id
Recommendation: Use Chrome's built-in Task Manager (Shift+Esc) to identify the specific tab/extension responsible and close or disable it.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
CPU and disk both spike briefly every week at the same time for no obvious reason

The weekly Scheduled Defrag/optimize task was running (it also does TRIM on SSDs, which is normal and beneficial), accounting for the periodic CPU/disk activity.
Commands used:
- Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName '\Microsoft\Windows\Defrag\ScheduledDefrag' | Select-Object LastRunTime
Recommendation: This is expected maintenance; no action needed unless you want to reschedule it to an idle time via Optimize Drives.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (cpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
CPU-Z / Task Manager shows the CPU stuck at its lowest possible frequency all the time

The CPU is pinned near its minimum frequency regardless of load, most commonly caused by the active power plan's 'Maximum processor state' being capped low, or a laptop stuck in a battery-saver-like state even on AC power.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object CurrentClockSpeed, MaxClockSpeed
Recommendation: Check Power Options > Change plan settings > Advanced > Processor power management > Maximum processor state, and set it to 100% for both On battery and Plugged in.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
GPU usage shows 100% in Task Manager even sitting idle on the desktop

A background browser tab with hardware-accelerated video decode running (e.g., an autoplay video) was pinning the GPU's video-decode engine, which Task Manager rolls up into overall GPU usage.
Commands used:
- Get-Counter '\GPU Engine(*)\Utilization Percentage' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty CounterSamples | Where-Object CookedValue -gt 50
Recommendation: Close or pause background video tabs; if it persists with nothing obviously playing, disable hardware acceleration in the browser as a test.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Games stutter noticeably even though both CPU and GPU usage show under 60%

Neither the CPU nor GPU is actually maxed out, which points away from a raw performance bottleneck and toward a driver-level frame-pacing issue -- the installed GPU driver is notably out of date.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | Select-Object Name, DriverVersion
Recommendation: Update to the latest vendor GPU driver (clean install) and check the game's frame-rate cap/V-Sync settings, which commonly cause this exact symptom.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
The GPU fan doesn't spin at all even under heavy gaming load

Windows reports the GPU itself as healthy, but modern GPUs use a 'zero RPM' fan mode that keeps fans off below a temperature threshold -- normal unless the card is also thermal throttling.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | Select-Object Name, Status
Recommendation: Check the actual GPU temperature in the vendor's control panel (GeForce Experience/Adrenalin); fans should spin up once it crosses roughly 50-60C. If they never spin even when hot, that's a hardware fault worth servicing.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Getting repeated 'Display driver stopped responding and has recovered' errors

Repeated TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery) events confirm the GPU driver is timing out and being reset by Windows, typically from an unstable/overclocked GPU, an outdated driver, or insufficient power delivery.
Commands used:
- Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; ProviderName='Display'; Id=4101} -MaxEvents 3
Recommendation: Reset any GPU overclock to stock, do a clean driver reinstall with DDU, and confirm the PSU meets the card's rated wattage.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Games are using the integrated graphics instead of the dedicated GPU, performance is terrible

Both GPUs are healthy and present, but Windows Graphics Settings had the game's preference set to 'Power saving' (integrated), rather than routing it to the dedicated GPU.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | Select-Object Name, Status
Recommendation: Go to Settings > System > Display > Graphics, add the game's .exe, and set it to 'High performance' to force the dedicated GPU.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
The dedicated GPU is not detected at all, Device Manager shows Code 43

Code 43 means Windows detected the GPU but the driver reported it as failed, which is commonly caused by a corrupted driver install, an unstable overclock, or in some cases a failing card.
Commands used:
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Display | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName, ProblemCode
Recommendation: Clean reinstall the driver with DDU in Safe Mode; if Code 43 persists on a fresh driver and default clocks, the card itself may be failing and should be tested in another system.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
External GPU enclosure isn't recognized when connected over Thunderbolt

The Thunderbolt controller itself is fine, but the eGPU enclosure never enumerated as a display device, which usually means Thunderbolt device authorization is blocking it or it wasn't connected before boot.
Commands used:
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Display | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
Recommendation: Check Thunderbolt security settings (set to 'No Security' or approve the device once), and connect/power on the eGPU before waking or booting the laptop.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Video editing software crashes with an out-of-memory-style error during exports

The GPU's dedicated video memory (VRAM) is being fully consumed during export, which causes the crash -- a project-complexity/VRAM-capacity issue, not a driver bug.
Commands used:
- Get-Counter '\GPU Process Memory(*)\Dedicated Usage' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty CounterSamples | Sort-Object CookedValue -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
Recommendation: Lower the export/preview resolution or proxy settings, close other GPU-heavy apps during export, or consider a GPU with more VRAM for these project sizes.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Laptop with two GPUs sometimes runs games on the wrong one and battery drains fast

Both GPUs are healthy; the issue is the per-app GPU preference in Windows Graphics Settings, which for this game defaults to 'Let Windows decide' and picks the integrated GPU inconsistently.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | Select-Object Name, Status
Recommendation: Explicitly set the game to 'High performance' (dedicated GPU) under Settings > System > Display > Graphics rather than relying on automatic switching.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Seeing visual glitches and corrupted textures on screen, especially in games

TDR/reset events correlate with the visible artifacts, pointing to an unstable GPU (often from a memory overclock, aging VRAM, or an outdated driver) rather than a game-specific bug.
Commands used:
- Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; ProviderName='Display'} -MaxEvents 5
Recommendation: Reset any GPU/VRAM overclock to default, run a GPU stress/memory test, and reinstall the driver clean; persistent artifacts at stock settings suggest failing VRAM.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
The GPU crashes specifically when exporting video with hardware encoding enabled

The crash coincides with a TDR reset during hardware encoding; the installed driver is a Game Ready release, which is validated primarily for gaming, not sustained encoder workloads.
Commands used:
- Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; ProviderName='Display'; Id=4101} -MaxEvents 3
Recommendation: Switch to the vendor's 'Studio'/creator driver branch if available, and lower the encoder preset/quality setting to reduce load during export.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Games run fine plugged in but are much slower and choppier on battery

This is expected behavior on gaming laptops: the dedicated GPU is deliberately clocked down on battery power to preserve runtime, unrelated to any fault.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | Select-Object Name, Status
Recommendation: If you need full performance unplugged, check the vendor's GPU control panel for an option to disable battery-power throttling, understanding it will drain the battery much faster.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
GPU driver installer fails or rolls back every time partway through

Remnants of a previous GPU driver installation were conflicting with the new install, causing it to fail partway through and roll back.
Commands used:
- Get-WinEvent -LogName Application -FilterXPath "*[System[Provider[@Name='MsiInstaller']]]" -MaxEvents 3
Recommendation: Fully remove the existing driver with Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) in Safe Mode, reboot, then install the new driver on a clean slate.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
GPU usage sits at 0-20% during gameplay while CPU is at 100%, framerate is still bad

The CPU is fully saturated while the GPU is mostly idle, meaning the CPU is the actual bottleneck for this game/settings combo -- more GPU power wouldn't help here.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object LoadPercentage
Recommendation: Lower CPU-bound settings (draw distance, NPC/physics density, background apps) rather than upgrading the GPU; closing background CPU-heavy apps often helps immediately.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
GPU fans spin up and usage stays high even when no games or apps are open

An unrecognized process with a name mimicking a system process was found driving GPU load with nothing else open -- consistent with unauthorized cryptomining/malware, not a legitimate app.
Commands used:
- Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 Name, Id
Recommendation: Do not assume it's safe. Run a full Microsoft Defender offline scan immediately and remove the process/startup entry if confirmed malicious; consider a second-opinion scan from another reputable tool.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (gpu) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
A newly installed GPU performs far below its expected benchmarks

The GPU is correctly detected and healthy at the OS level; underperformance versus expected benchmarks is most commonly caused by the card negotiating a lower PCIe link speed/width (e.g., x4 instead of x16) rather than a driver or Windows issue.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | Select-Object Name, AdapterRAM
Recommendation: Check the PCIe slot and link speed/width reported in the vendor's GPU utility (e.g., GPU-Z); reseat the card fully in a full x16 slot and ensure the slot isn't bandwidth-limited by another installed device.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (boot) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
PC won't boot, stops with a blue screen saying INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE

Bugcheck 0x7B (INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE) indicates Windows lost access to the boot volume at startup, most often after a storage controller mode change (AHCI/RAID/NVMe) in BIOS or a failed storage driver update.
Commands used:
- Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; Id=41} -MaxEvents 1
Recommendation: Boot into Recovery > Advanced options > Command Prompt and run 'bootrec /fixboot' and 'bootrec /rebuildbcd'; if it started after a BIOS change, revert the SATA/NVMe mode back to what Windows was installed under.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (boot) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
PC boots straight into 'Automatic Repair' every time and loops back to it

SrtTrail.txt from the recovery log pointed to a corrupt boot-critical driver file, causing Automatic Repair to fail and loop instead of completing.
Commands used:
- Get-Content 'X:\Windows\System32\LogFiles\Srt\SrtTrail.txt' -Tail 5
Recommendation: From Recovery > Command Prompt, run 'sfc /scannow' targeting the offline OS or 'DISM /Image:C:\ /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth'; if that fails, disable automatic repair temporarily with 'bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No' to boot and investigate further.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (boot) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Getting 'The Boot Configuration Data file is missing some required information'

The BCD store itself is missing or corrupted, so Windows can't find valid boot entries to load from.
Commands used:
- bcdedit /enum all
Recommendation: From Recovery > Command Prompt run 'bootrec /rebuildbcd'; if it finds no Windows installations, rebuild manually with 'bcdboot C:\Windows'.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (boot) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Boot error: 'winload.efi is missing or contains errors'

The boot loader file winload.efi is missing from the System32 folder, which UEFI needs to hand off into Windows -- the BCD entry can't complete the boot chain.
Commands used:
- Test-Path 'C:\Windows\System32\winload.efi'
Recommendation: Rebuild the boot files from Recovery > Command Prompt with 'bootrec /rebuildbcd' followed by 'bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI' (where S: is the EFI system partition).
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (boot) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
PC won't boot after enabling Secure Boot, error about an untrusted boot loader

Secure Boot is active and rejecting the current boot loader/driver signature (common right after a dual-boot Linux install or an unsigned driver) -- the protection is working as designed rather than a fault.
Commands used:
- Confirm-SecureBootUEFI
Recommendation: Either re-enable a Microsoft-signed boot path (repair Windows Boot Manager) or, if you intentionally need unsigned boot components, disable Secure Boot in BIOS/UEFI.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (boot) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
'Missing operating system' error on a BIOS/legacy boot drive

The Master Boot Record on the boot drive was damaged or overwritten, so the BIOS couldn't hand off to Windows. Rewriting a fresh, standard MBR is a safe first fix.
Commands used:
- bootrec /fixmbr
Recommendation: Follow with 'bootrec /fixboot' and 'bootrec /rebuildbcd'; if a dual-boot loader (GRUB) was overwritten, you'll need to restore it separately.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (boot) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Disk shows as a GPT Protective Partition and Windows won't boot from it

The disk's GPT partition table header is unreadable (reporting RAW instead of GPT), which prevents the firmware from locating the EFI/boot partitions.
Commands used:
- Get-Disk | Select-Object Number, PartitionStyle, OperationalStatus
Recommendation: This needs partition-table-level recovery (e.g., a read-only scan with a tool like TestDisk to rebuild the GPT) before the disk is bootable again; back up data first if any read access is still possible.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance (boot) problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
'No bootable device found' and the EFI system partition seems to be gone

The EFI System Partition (which holds the Windows Boot Manager) is missing from the partition table, so firmware has nothing to hand off to.
Commands used:
- Get-Partition | Select-Object DiskNumber, PartitionNumber, GptType
Recommendation: From Recovery > Command Prompt, create a new FAT32 EFI partition with diskpart and run 'bcdboot C:\Windows /s <EFI drive letter> /f UEFI' to repopulate it.
